text: The three contracts ADR-001 affects (auth-api@v1, profile-api@v1, profile-api@v2) name it only in a body line, not in governed_by front matter. Gate C3 reports this as a warning today and as an error in any step that changes ADR-001's file or one of those contracts (seen in S02's gate run). Add governed_by: [ADR-001] to each contract's front matter (hsdd-adr Bidirectional Linking), whether ADR-001 is amended or superseded.

hsdd/management/2026-10-30-execution-plan.md routes C-2 (finding F-3): add simple-login to ADR-001's affects, since hsdd/spec/simple-login.md carries Governed by: [ADR-001]. It is a link fix with no decision and no dependency: absorb it in this update and cite C-2, or leave it to that plan; record which (DEC-016).

hsdd/management/2026-10-30-execution-plan.md routes C-3 (finding F-4): add the web phases that read auth-api@v1's fixtures to its consumers. Absorb it in this touch and cite C-3, or leave it to that plan; record which (DEC-016).

Leave profile-api@v1 as it is: its move to deprecated is C-1 of hsdd/management/2026-10-30-execution-plan.md, which waits on the owner's Sync A answer to A-1 (the sunset date). This touch changes profile-api@v2 only (DEC-016).

note: governed_by: [ADR-001] added after owner in the front matter of hsdd/contract/auth-api.md, profile-api.md and profile-api.v2.md; body lines, Versioning, schemas and fixtures untouched, versions unchanged (DEC-023). Gate C3 reports nothing for the three contracts.

C-2 absorbed: simple-login added to ADR-001's affects in the same edit as booking-api@v1, cited in the Amendments entry with C-2 and F-3 (DEC-022). The execution plan's C-2 checkbox is left for the next checkpoint to tick.

text: ADR-001 is amended, not superseded (DEC-018, DEC-019): booking-api@v1 takes auth-api@v1's bearer token from the in-memory store; sessions are never in PostgreSQL; there is no logout endpoint. Its Consequences make a missing, unknown or expired token one case at every endpoint that takes the token, 401 UNAUTHORIZED, so booking-api@v1's endpoints answer it with the same envelope profile-api gives. ADR-001's affects already names booking-api@v1: its front matter needs governed_by: [ADR-001, ADR-002], or gate C3's forward-reference warning becomes an error once the file exists.

ADR-001 keeps in-memory sessions and client-side sign-out (DEC-018, DEC-019), so its update asks nothing of auth-api@v1's guarantees on a restart or sign-out beyond what they already rest on. If the touch restates the token guarantee ('accepted ... until expiresAt'), a restart ending every token early is existing behavior (ADR-001 Consequences, first bullet), a clarification rather than a new rule. auth-api@v1's front matter already carries governed_by: [ADR-001] (Q-001).

ADR-001's affects now names simple-login (execution plan C-2, DEC-022), so the root header must keep Governed by: [ADR-001] when the touch restates it, or gate C3 errors. The Decisions bullet on ADR-001 (in-memory sessions, 30 minutes, sign-out on the client) stays true under the amendment.

ADR-001 keeps sessions in memory (DEC-018), so simple-login.integration.2's restart stays a valid expired-token stand-in for AC-2.3 and the intake record's 'revisited if ADR-001's update makes sessions survive a restart' does not fire. The PRD v2 Success test that a restart keeps every booking must sign in again after the restart, since the same restart signs every user out (ADR-001 Consequences).
